body: **Foco:** Verbo-chave: have.
**Pronúncia:** Ajuste refinado de entonação.
**24 palavras novas** (discurso público).
**Texto do dia:** editorial / opinião.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo usar have em seus sentidos centrais (have lunch, have to, have something done, have trouble doing) para falar de participação pública.

body: Esta aula treina **responder em frases completas (IELTS Speaking, TOEFL Speaking)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Editorial: Let Residents Have a Say
paras: Residents of the Ninth District **have to** wait weeks to learn what the council has decided. When the Riverside Plan was **published**, many **had trouble** finding the document at all; some **had it printed** at a copy shop, and others simply **gave up**.

This is not how a city should **have a conversation** with its people. The council **has the report translated**, the hearing **recorded** and the minutes **posted**, yet **has lunch** with developers before any vote. It should **have nothing to hide**.
We urge the mayor to **have a public meeting** each month and **have every proposal reviewed** by an independent panel. Citizens **have a right** to know; they should not **have to ask twice**.

items.q: The council has lunch with developers.
The editorial wants monthly public meetings.
items.why: have a public meeting each month.

rows: Residents **have to** wait. / They **don’t have to** ask.

blocks.body: **Have + objeto + particípio** = mandar/ter algo feito por outro. **Have trouble + -ing** (sem *in*). **Have to** = obrigação; **don’t have to** = não é preciso.
*Don’t have to* ≠ *mustn’t*: o primeiro é dispensa, o segundo é proibição.

items.s: The council ___ the report translated. (have, presente)
Citizens should not ___ to ask twice. (have)
The mayor ___ lunch with developers. (have, presente)

body: **Have a say** — ter voz
**Have nothing to hide** — não ter nada a esconder
**Have a word with** — trocar uma palavra com
**Have second thoughts** — ter dúvidas
**Have the upper hand** — levar vantagem
**Have a point** — ter razão
**Have a lot on one’s plate** — estar sobrecarregado
**Have it both ways** — querer as duas coisas
**Have no choice but to** — não ter escolha senão
**Have an axe to grind** — ter segundas intenções
**I had trouble finding the plan online.** — Tive dificuldade para achar o plano online.
**Do I have to pay for it?** — Preciso pagar por ela?
**We can have a copy printed for you.** — Podemos mandar imprimir uma cópia para você.

prompts.q: Distinguish don’t have to and mustn’t.
prompts.model: You don’t have to pay, but you mustn’t forget to sign.

blocks.task: Write 5 sentences about a public service, using have to, have something done, have trouble doing and have lunch.
blocks.model: Citizens have to queue for hours to renew a permit. Many have trouble understanding the forms. The office has the notices translated into three languages. Officials should not have lunch with applicants during a review. Every resident should have a right to a clear answer.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
